25163-at-good-old-siwash.title: At Good Old Siwash
25163-at-good-old-siwash.creator: Unknown
25163-at-good-old-siwash.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Am I going to the game Saturday? Am I going to eat some more food this year? Am I going to draw my pay this month? Am I going to do any more breathing after I get this lungful used up? All foolish questions, pal.

77456-geological-and-solar-climates.title: A Thesis.
77456-geological-and-solar-climates.creator: Unknown
77456-geological-and-solar-climates.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. en one comes forward with some skillfully carved jewel which he has wrought into shape to deck his shrine. Sometimes it is only a little piece merely good for inlaying the walls, yet it fits well in its place and strengthens the faith of other workers. Again it is the great keystone for some massive arch whose other stones were laid in bygone times.

7968-lying-prophets-a-novel.title: Lying Prophets A Novel
7968-lying-prophets-a-novel.creator: Unknown
7968-lying-prophets-a-novel.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. es and ginger-beer bottles in them; little shops; little doors, at which cluster little children and many cats, the latter mostly tortoise-shell and white. Infants watch their elders playing marbles in the roadway, and the cats stretch lazy bodies on the mats, made of old fishing-net, which lie at every cottage door.

arxiv-2007-12081.title: NITS-Hinglish-SentiMix at SemEval-2020 Task 9: Sentiment Analysis For Code-Mixed Social Media Text Using an Ensemble Model
arxiv-2007-12081.creator: Subhra Jyoti Baroi Nivedita Singh Ringki Das Thoudam Doren Singh
arxiv-2007-12081.description: Abstract Sentiment Analysis is the process of deciphering what a sentence emotes and classifying them as either positive, negative, or neutral. In recent times, India has seen a huge influx in the number of active social media users and this has led to a plethora of unstructured text data.

arxiv-2009-00466.title: toki: A Build- and Test-Platform for Prototyping and Evaluating Operating System Concepts in Real-Time Environments Thanks: This work was supported by the European Union (EU) under the Horizon 2020 program, projects TAPPS (Trusted Apps for open CPSs) and 5GCroCo (5G Cross Border Control), and the Ge
arxiv-2009-00466.creator: Oliver Horst, Uwe Baumgarten
arxiv-2009-00466.description: Abstract Typically, even low-level operating systemconcepts, such as resource sharing strategies and predictability measures, are evaluated with Linux on PC hardware. This leaves a large gap to real industrial applications. Hence, the direct transfer of the results might be difficult. As a solution, we present toki , a prototyping and evaluation platform based on FreeRTOS and several open-source libraries.

arxiv-2107-04670.title: Quantum dots as a probe of fundamental physics:
arxiv-2107-04670.creator: Deviation from exponential decay law
arxiv-2107-04670.description: Abstract We explore a possibility of measuring deviation from the exponential decay law in pure quantum systems. The power law behavior at late times of decay time profile is predicted in quantum mechanics, and has been experimentally attempted to detect, but with failures except a claim in an open system.

arxiv-2205-10201.title: On the Decentralization of Blockchain-enabled Asynchronous Federated Learning Thanks: This work was funded by the IN CERCA grant from the Secretaria d’Universitats i Recerca del departament d’Empresa i Coneixement de la Generalitat de Catalunya, and partially by the Spanish project PID2020-113832RB-
arxiv-2205-10201.creator: Francesc Wilhelmi, Elia Guerra, Paolo Dini
arxiv-2205-10201.description: Abstract Federated learning (FL), thanks in part to the emergence of the edge computing paradigm, is expected to enable true real-time applications in production environments. However, its original dependence on a central server for orchestration raises several concerns in terms of security, privacy, and scalability.

arxiv-2210-15396.title: Quantum security of subset cover problems This work was partially funded by PEPR integrated project EPiQ ANR-22-PETQ-0007 part of Plan France 2030.
arxiv-2210-15396.creator: Samuel Bouaziz–Ermann, Alex B. Grilo, Damien Vergnaud
arxiv-2210-15396.description: Abstract The subset cover problem for k ≥ 1 k\geq 1 hash functions, which can be seen as an extension of the collision problem, was introduced in 2002 by Reyzin and Reyzin to analyse the security of their hash-function based signature scheme HORS.

arxiv-2310-00324.title: An Interfacial Profile-Preserving Approach for Phase Field Modeling of Incompressible Two-Phase Flows
arxiv-2310-00324.creator: Haohao Hao, Xiangwei Li, Chenglin Jiang, Huanshu Tan
arxiv-2310-00324.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce an interfacial profile-preserving approach for phase field modeling for simulating incompressible two-phase flows. While the advective Cahn-Hilliard equation effectively captures the topological evolution of complex interfacial structures, it tends to displace the fluid interface from its equilibrium state, impacting simulation accuracy.

arxiv-2403-05100.title: Exploring the Adversarial Frontier: Quantifying Robustness via Adversarial Hypervolume
arxiv-2403-05100.creator: Ping Guo, Cheng Gong, Xi Lin, Zhiyuan Yang, Qingfu Zhang
arxiv-2403-05100.description: Abstract The escalating threat of adversarial attacks on deep learning models, particularly in security-critical fields, has highlighted the need for robust deep learning systems. Conventional evaluation methods of their robustness have relied on adversarial accuracy, which measures the model performance under a specific perturbation intensity.

arxiv-2404-19120.title: Computing distances on Riemann surfaces
arxiv-2404-19120.creator: Huck Stepanyants, Alan Beardon, Jeremy Paton, Dmitri Krioukov
arxiv-2404-19120.description: Abstract Riemann surfaces are among the simplest and most basic geometric objects. They appear as key players in many branches of physics, mathematics, and other sciences. Despite their widespread significance, how to compute distances between pairs of points on compact Riemann surfaces is surprisingly unknown, unless the surface is a sphere or a torus.

arxiv-2410-00341.title: Effects of Systematic Error on Quantum-Enhanced Atom Interferometry
arxiv-2410-00341.creator: Joshua Goldsmith, Joseph Hope, Simon Haine
arxiv-2410-00341.description: Abstract We develop a framework for describing the effects of systematic state preparation error in quantum-enhanced atom interferometry on sensing performance. We do this in the context of both spin-squeezed and non-Gaussian states for the two-axis-twisting (TAT), one-axis-twisting (OAT), and twist-and-turn (TNT) state preparation schemes, and derive general conditions for robustness and susceptibility of quantum states to state preparation error.

arxiv-2412-08479.title: CAT : Class Aware Adaptive Thresholding for Semi-Supervised Domain Generalization
arxiv-2412-08479.creator: Sumaiya Zoha, Jeong-Gun Lee, Young-Woong Ko
arxiv-2412-08479.description: Abstract Domain Generalization (DG) seeks to transfer knowledge from multiple source domains to unseen target domains, even in the presence of domain shifts. Achieving effective generalization typically requires a large and diverse set of labeled source data to learn robust representations that can generalize to new, unseen domains.

arxiv-2503-02629.title: On-Demand Pulse Shaping with Partially Coherent Pulses in Nonlinear Dispersive Media
arxiv-2503-02629.creator: Qian Chen, Yanlin Bai, Xiaohan Wang, Peipei Pengcor1, Jingsong Liucor1, Yangjian Caicor1, Chunhao Liangcor1
arxiv-2503-02629.description: Abstract In this Letter, we employ the complex screen method to investigate the dynamic evolution of partially coherent pulses with specified properties as they propagate through a nonlinear Kerr medium. Our results reveal that partially coherent pulses can retain stable pulse characteristics and exhibit enhanced robustness when the source coherence is reduced.

arxiv-2505-19025.title: SQUiD: Synthesizing Relational Databases from Unstructured Text
arxiv-2505-19025.creator: Mushtari Sadia, Zhenning Yang, Yunming Xiao, Amrita Roy Chowdhury
arxiv-2505-19025.description: Abstract Relational databases are central to modern data management, yet most data exists in unstructured forms like text documents. To bridge this gap, we leverage large language models (LLMs) to automatically synthesize a relational database by generating its schema and populating its tables from raw text.

arxiv-2511-19592.title: On decoding the string from interfaces in 2d conformal field theories Preprint: CCTP-2025-14 ITCP-2025-14
arxiv-2511-19592.creator: Avik Banerjee, Tanay Kibe, Ayan Mukhopadhyay, and Giuseppe Policastro
arxiv-2511-19592.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Avik Banerjee, Tanay Kibe, Ayan Mukhopadhyay, and Giuseppe Policastro. General solutions of a gravitational junction between two copies of a three-dimensional Einstein manifold ℳ \mathcal{M} correspond to the solutions of the non-linear Nambu-Goto equation for a string in ℳ \mathcal{M} .

pmc-10547155.title: Safety outcomes when switching between biosimilars and reference biologics: A systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-10547155.creator: Thomas M Herndon, Cristina Ausin, Nina N Brahme, Sarah J Schrieber, Michelle Luo, Frances C Andrada, Carol Kim, Wanjie Sun, Lingjie Zhou, Stella Grosser, Sarah Yim, M Stacey Ricci, Enrique Teran, Enrique Teran, Enrique Teran, Enrique Teran
pmc-10547155.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Biosimilars are increasingly available for the treatment of many serious disorders, however some concerns persist about switching a patient to a biosimilar whose condition is stable while on the reference biologic. Randomized controlled studies and extension studies with a switch treatment period (STP) to or from a biosimilar and its reference biologic were identified from publicly available information maintained by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

pmc-10583739.title: Immune-related Adverse Events after Immune Checkpoint Blockade–based Therapy Are Associated with Improved Survival in Advanced Sarcomas
pmc-10583739.creator: Evan Rosenbaum, Kenneth Seier, Martina Bradic, Ciara Kelly, Sujana Movva, Benjamin A. Nacev, Mrinal M. Gounder, Mary L. Keohan, Viswatej Avutu, Ping Chi, Katherine A. Thornton, Jason E. Chan, Mark A. Dickson, Mark T.A. Donoghue, William D. Tap, Li-Xuan Qin, Sandra P. D'Angelo
pmc-10583739.description: The association between immune-related AEs (irAE) and outcome in patients with sarcoma is not known. We retrospectively reviewed a cohort of patients with advanced sarcoma treated with immune checkpoint blockade (ICB)-based therapy. Association of irAEs with survival was assessed using a Cox regression model that incorporated irAE occurrence as a time-dependent covariate.

pmc-10645192.title: Research Advances on Deafness Genes Associated with Mitochondrial tRNA-37 Modifications
pmc-10645192.creator: Panpan Bian, Jing Chai, Baicheng Xu
pmc-10645192.description: As the most common cause of speech disorders, the etiological study of deafness is important for the diagnosis and treatment of deafness. The mitochondrial genome has gradually become a hotspot for deafness genetic research. Mitochondria are the core organelles of energy and material metabolism in eukaryotic cells.

pmc-11367042.title: Synthesis and Characterization of Cr doped CeO2 nanoparticles for Rhodamine B dye degradation
pmc-11367042.creator: Veena B, Seetha M
pmc-11367042.description: The main aim of this work is to synthesis and study Cr doped CeO2 nanoparticles for Rhodamine B dye degradation. In this regard, 2 wt% and 4 wt% Cr doped CeO2 nanoparticles were successfully synthesized through a simple chemical precipitation method. The structural characteristics and elemental composition of the synthesized samples were analyzed using XRD and XPS techniques.

pmc-11513634.title: In vitro resistance development gives insights into molecular resistance mechanisms against cefiderocol
pmc-11513634.creator: Richard Kriz, Kathrin Spettel, Alina Pichler, Katharina Schefberger, Maria Sanz-Codina, Felix Lötsch, Nicole Harrison, Birgit Willinger, Markus Zeitlinger, Heinz Burgmann, Heimo Lagler
pmc-11513634.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Cefiderocol, a novel siderophore cephalosporin, demonstrates promising in vitro activity against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, including carbapenemase-producing strains. Nonetheless, only a few reports are available regarding the acquisition of resistance in clinical settings, primarily due to its recent usage. This study aimed to investigate cefiderocol resistance using an in vitro resistance development model to gain insights into the underlying molecular resistance mechanisms.

pmc-11613752.title: Transforming nursing work environments: the impact of organizational culture on work-related stress among nurses: a systematic review
pmc-11613752.creator: Evans Kasmai Kiptulon, Mohammed Elmadani, Godfrey Mbaabu Limungi, Klara Simon, Lívia Tóth, Eva Horvath, Anna Szőllősi, Dahabo Adi Galgalo, Orsolya Maté, Adrienn Ujváriné Siket
pmc-11613752.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundCreating a healthy and conducive nursing work environment is a universal global nursing concern. Work-Related Stress, global nursing and a public health problem that has continued to bedevil the world healthcare systems is of a particular interest. It has not only compromised the quality of patient care but also negatively impacted nurses’ quality of work life and adversely affected global healthcare management. Organizational culture is an important determinant of nurses’ work-related stress, yet it remains systematically under-researched.

pmc-11644837.title: Analytical Design and Polyphase Implementation Technique for 2D Digital FIR Differentiators
pmc-11644837.creator: Radu Matei, Doru Florin Chiper
pmc-11644837.description: In this work, an analytical method in the frequency domain is proposed for the design of two-dimensional digital FIR differentiators. This technique uses an approximation based on two methods: the Chebyshev series and the Fourier series, which, finally, lead to a trigonometric polynomial, which is a remarkably precise approximation of the transfer function of the ideal differentiator.

pmc-12579251.title: Lithium diffusion-controlled Li-Al alloy negative electrode for all-solid-state battery
pmc-12579251.creator: Yuju Jeon, Dong Ju Lee, Hongkui Zheng, Sesha Sai Behara, Jung-Pil Lee, Junlin Wu, Feng Li, Wei Tang, Lanshuang Zhang, Yu-Ting Chen, Dapeng Xu, Jiyoung Kim, Min-Sang Song, Anton Van der Ven, Kai He, Zheng Chen
pmc-12579251.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Metal alloy negative electrodes are promising candidates for lithium all-solid-state batteries due to their high specific capacity and low cost. However, chemo-mechanical degradation and atomic transport limitations in the solid state remain unresolved challenges. Herein, we demonstrate a lithium-aluminum alloy negative electrode design (LixAl1, x = molar ratio of lithium to aluminum) based on a comprehensive understanding of the underlying diffusion mechanisms within the lithium-poor α (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.05) and lithium-rich β phases (0.95 ≤ x ≤ 1).

pmc-12751538.title: Associations between sleep duration with depression and the mediating role of physical activity in patients with chronic respiratory diseases: evidence from three nationwide population-based studies
pmc-12751538.creator: Yuanhao Tong, Huayu Li, Mingrui Duan, Qinyuan He, Ziang Gao
pmc-12751538.description: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), asthma, and asthma-COPD overlap (ACO) are common chronic respiratory diseases that could cause severe mental disorders. Sleep duration and physical activity (PA) are related to depression in various diseases. However, their roles in patients with chronic respiratory diseases remain unknown.

pmc-13008846.title: The guardian of the genome meets immunotherapy: p53-based strategies
pmc-13008846.creator: Tatyana A. Savostyanova, Julia A. Lopatnikova, Sergey V. Sennikov
pmc-13008846.description: Originally reported as an oncogene and currently known to be a major “genome guardian”, the p53 protein remains one of the most explored transcription factors, exhibiting variety of functions both within transcription regulation and beyond. Given that p53 dysfunction contributes to the majority of human cancers, understanding its regulatory mechanisms and therapeutic potential remains a primary research focus.

pmc-13457002.title: Infrared thermography in clinically healthy dogs shows body region and haircoat variability
pmc-13457002.creator: Nathan Hall, Amber Hall, Lainey Atwood, Jessica Petry, Melissa J. Lewis

pmc-13594369.title: Characterizing particle size in agricultural runoff to inform stormwater basin design
pmc-13594369.creator: Michael A Holly, Andrew J Votis, Mason Anderson‐Giles, Kpoti M Gunn
pmc-13594369.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Upper US Midwest sediment‐basin design commonly relies on parent‐soil texture classes and texture‐based settling‐velocity defaults (Natural Resources Conservation Service Conservation Practice Standard Code 350), yet conservation‐managed fields can export fine particles that bypass gravity settling. Runoff from 13 edge‐of‐field watersheds in Wisconsin and Indiana showed systematic divergence between particle size distribution representations: volume‐weighted (mass‐based) D50 ≈ 30 µm (coarser classification) versus number‐weighted (count‐based) D50 ≈ 3.5 µm (clay‐rich suspension).

pmc-13681313.title: When flexibility outpaces safety: rethinking pregnancy screening in random-start ovarian stimulation
pmc-13681313.creator: Randy Morris
pmc-13681313.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Random-start ovarian stimulation (RSOS) protocols represent a genuine clinical advance, offering scheduling flexibility that benefits both patients and clinics (1). But their adoption has quietly narrowed a margin of safety that was rarely tested before. Early-follicular-phase stimulation, usually on cycle days 2–3, required a defined menstrual event before treatment began, and was typically paired with a baseline blood test and ultrasound—a combination that, together with the bleed itself, made an unrecognized pregnancy or an inadvertent luteal-phase start extremely unlikely.
